acceptance: A test with two branches that change different files, where the second is stale against the base and conflicts with it, shows no 'coordinate before landing' warning for the first branch (option a), or shows wording that names the base branch as the other side (option b).
A test with two branches that change the same lines still warns and names the shared file.
The chosen option and its reason are recorded on this item, and `make pr-open` still succeeds when the scan itself fails.
description:
`make pr-open` for PR #4170 printed: `textual conflict with PR #3916 (chore/seed-corpus-20261101-3095) in publication/ledger-seed.json, results-data/corpus-inventory.json — coordinate before landing`. PR #4170 changed nine files, none of them those two, and merged without conflict.

Cause, read from `make/pr-landing.mk` (`pr-conflict-scan`): for every open pull request against `develop` it runs `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only HEAD origin/<branch>` and reports any conflict. `HEAD` contains current `develop`, so a branch that is merely stale against `develop` conflicts with every fresh branch, whatever that branch changed. The warning then tells an unrelated author to coordinate. It repeats on every `pr-open` while the stale pull request stays open.

Decision gate. Choose one and record why: (a) report a conflict only when a conflicting file is also in this branch's diff against the merge base with `develop`; or (b) keep the scan and reword the line to say the other pull request conflicts with `develop`. Prefer (a) unless authors use the stale-branch signal.

Guardrails.
- The scan stays advisory: `pr-open` calls it with `|| true`, and it must not become a refusal.
- It must not add GitHub REST calls; the shared quota is already exhausted at times (pr-arm-github-rate-limit-backoff-20261112). Note that it also fetches every open branch.
- `make/monolith-baseline.json` records the recipe text; update it through the repository's own regeneration step, not by hand.
